news.title: OCC Finalizes Stablecoin Rule, Leaving Third-Party Rewards Under Review
news.body: The OCC finalized its GENIUS Act implementation rule, effective January 18, 2027, prohibiting issuers from directly paying stablecoin yield. Third-party reward arrangements remain subject to case-by-case evaluation; the distinction between issuance and distribution does not give wallet providers or distributors blanket permission to offer incentives. Separate rulemaking will address BSA, AML and sanctions requirements.

news.title: Amex Announces 3,500 Job Cuts as Quarterly Card Spending Reaches $454 Billion
news.body: American Express announced approximately 3,500 job cuts alongside third-quarter revenue of $20 billion, up 9%, and billed business of $454 billion, up 8% on an FX-adjusted basis. Management emphasized automation and expense management amid competition from Ramp and Brex, and plans to add agents to its commercial platform. The announcement pairs workforce reductions with growing card spending; it does not establish that AI directly caused every eliminated role.

news.title: Slingshot Raises $27 Million for Insurance Sold at Checkout
news.body: Minneapolis-based Slingshot Insurance emerged from stealth with $27 million in seed funding, co-led by Rally Ventures and Skyward Group, Crunchbase News reported. The company plans to develop small insurance policies sold at checkout, adding insurance distribution to merchant purchase flows. The funding announcement does not establish live merchant integrations, premium volume or underwriting economics.

news.title: Citi Restricts External Agents While Expanding Embedded Corporate Banking
news.body: Corporate clients can pilot self-initiated U.S. account opening through CitiDirect as Citi develops embedded banking experiences in SAP and Oracle. The bank nevertheless blocks external agentic access beyond certain existing read-only open-banking connections. Those embedded workflows therefore do not authorize third-party agents to initiate transactions or move money.

news.title: Parents Differ on Financing Costs and Monthly Payments When Choosing Credit
news.body: Pay-later research found that 34% of married parents prioritize monthly payment size, versus 26% prioritizing cost; single parents favor cost over payment size, 29% to 25%. BNPL availability was very or extremely influential in medical or dental provider selection for 47% of single parents, compared with 35% of married parents. These figures describe respondents’ stated preferences, not provider market-share gains. The research’s broader pay-later category includes regular credit-card payments and card installments alongside BNPL.
